newsitem.title: GERMANY: Zeitler-low interest rates do not mean cycle end.
newsitem.headline: Zeitler-low interest rates do not mean cycle end.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler said on Wednesday that even though key German interest rates are at historic lows, it need not be the end of the cycle for interest rate cuts.

"Even if the three leading German interest rates have reached historic lows, that does not mean the end of the line has been reached in the interest rate cycle," Zeitler said in a speech given at a banking conference.

Zeitler, who is president of the regional state central bank of Bavaria, went on to say that the "steady hand" approach to monetary policy means there is currently no need for monetary policy steps to be taken.

Money supply growth was appropriate when viewed over the long-term, Zeitler said, adding that the two-year trend on money supply growth was fitting, even if the M3 target corridor of four to seven percent was not reached by the end of 1996.
Zeitler said he saw positive growth expectations for the German economy, against the background of continuing problems in investment and in the jobs market.
Zeitler also said that a tough EU stability pact would inspire the market's confidence in the financial solidity of the fiscal policies of the various nation states.
